verdict.rationale: Pinecone's docs say a single index serves full-text search (BM25 token matching with Lucene query syntax over schema text fields, no model required) alongside semantic and sparse-vector search. Results are ranked via score_by text or query_string, so keyword search runs inside the database without a separate engine. A community user also notes the combined keyword+vector search. missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration of BM25/Lucene full-text quality and limits (tokenization, analyzers, field constraints).

support.subject: As a developer, I can run keyword/full-text search over documents inside the database without bolting on a separate search engine

citations.quote: A single index can serve full-text search (BM25 with Lucene queries), semantic search, and sparse-vector search together, often covering what previously required two indexes.
Full-text search is BM25 token matching with Lucene query syntax over text fields in your schema... No model required
When you search, you rank results via `score_by`: `text` (BM25), `query_string` (Lucene), `dense_vector`, or `sparse_vector`.
